howto.name: Meet the basic requirements
howto.text: Be at least 18 with a high school diploma or equivalent and a U.S. Social Security number.

howto.name: Complete the 63-hour pre-license course
howto.text: Finish Florida's state-approved 63-hour sales associate pre-license course and pass its end-of-course exam.

howto.name: Get fingerprinted
howto.text: Submit electronic fingerprints through a state-approved vendor for your background check.

howto.name: Apply to the DBPR
howto.text: Apply to the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation and receive your exam authorization.

howto.name: Pass the Florida state exam
howto.text: Pass the 100-question Florida sales associate exam (75% or higher) at a Pearson VUE testing center.

howto.name: Activate your license under a broker
howto.text: Join a licensed Florida broker, such as Adams, Cameron & Co., to activate your license and start working.

Oak Hill is the southernmost city in Volusia County, a quiet, rural community of about 2,100 people set along the Indian River and Mosquito Lagoon, near the Volusia and Brevard county line and the edge of the Space Coast. Here’s exactly how to get licensed, and what the local market looks like for a new agent.

How do you get a real estate license in Oak Hill?

You earn the Florida real estate sales associate license, valid statewide. There is no separate Oak Hill license. Be 18+ with a high school diploma, complete the 63-hour pre-license course, get fingerprinted, apply to the DBPR, pass the state exam (75% to pass), and activate under a broker. Most people finish in two to four months. Full detail is in our Florida licensing guide.

Is Oak Hill a good market for a new real estate agent?

Be honest with yourself about this one going in: Oak Hill is one of the smallest, quietest markets a new agent can choose in Volusia County. With a population of around 2,100, it is not a market with a lot of transactions on its own, and pretending otherwise would not serve you. What it offers instead is a distinct kind of property and a distinct kind of buyer, riverfront and lagoon-front homes, land, and a genuinely rural, low-density lifestyle a short drive from the Space Coast. Most agents who build a real business here work Oak Hill alongside neighboring southeast Volusia towns like Edgewater and New Smyrna Beach, rather than relying on Oak Hill transactions alone. Treated as a niche, low-volume market instead of a high-traffic one, it can be an honest place to build a career.

Oak Hill’s Timucua and Colonial heritage: a real local story

Oak Hill sits on land where the Timucua people lived for thousands of years. Seminole Rest National Historic Site, part of Canaveral National Seashore, lies on the edge of Mosquito Lagoon just east of town and preserves pre-Columbian shell middens and structures from that era. For an agent, this isn’t just historical trivia; it shapes the way some buyers think about the area. Buyers drawn to Oak Hill often want genuine, underdeveloped Florida, with real history, not a theme-park version of it. That story matters when you’re talking to someone who’s choosing waterfront land here versus developed strip-mall areas inland.

The Mosquito Lagoon: the Redfish Capital and why waterfront property sells differently

Mosquito Lagoon is known worldwide as the Redfish Capital of the World. Legendary flats fishing, both sport and commercial, has drawn anglers and fishing guides to Oak Hill for decades. That translates directly into a real estate market: buyers here aren’t just buying a house, they’re buying access to fishing. Properties with private docks, boat lifts, bayside bulkheads, and launch proximity command premiums that a developer-tract agent inland never encounters. Selling waterfront in Oak Hill means understanding tidal zones, inlet access, dock regulations, riparian rights, and the seasonal rhythms of both bonefish and red drum. Most new agents don’t develop this skill early, but in Oak Hill it’s a real, durable niche that sets you apart.

A smaller population, a more mature market

Oak Hill’s median age is about 59 years, with roughly a third of residents age 65 and older. This is a markedly older population than Volusia County as a whole. What that means for a real estate agent is a different buyer: less new-family first-time-home buying, more downsizing empty-nesters, retirees seeking waterfront or nature access without big-city prices, and active seniors who want boating and fishing in their backyard. The sales conversation shifts. You’re not selling school catchment areas and renovation upside; you’re selling peace, water access, and a slower pace. Understanding and respecting that buyer profile is not glamorous, but it’s honest work and it works.

Space Coast proximity: the NASA angle and the boating lifestyle

Oak Hill is the closest Volusia County community to Merritt Island National Wildlife Refuge and the Space Coast infrastructure, with Canaveral National Seashore forming the eastern boundary. That proximity creates a particular buyer profile: boaters and kayakers who want miles of scenic shoreline on the Indian River and Mosquito Lagoon without paying oceanfront prices. New Smyrna Beach is 15 minutes north, but a New Smyrna oceanfront property can cost double what a comparable waterfront home costs in Oak Hill. Buyers choosing Oak Hill are often making a deliberate choice: they want the water access, the fishing, the kayaking, and the nature without the resort noise and the resort price tag. That’s a real, sustainable market niche for an agent who understands it.

Does the brokerage you start with matter?

More than the town you pick. Your license must be held by a broker, and that brokerage decides your training, tools, and support in the make-or-break first year. A recognized local name carries real weight, and sellers trust it before you say a word.

Why start your real estate career with Adams, Cameron & Co.?

Adams, Cameron & Co. has been Volusia County’s largest brokerage since 1963, with around 300 agents and seven offices across Volusia and Flagler County, including Daytona Beach, Ormond Beachside, Ormond Mainland, Port Orange, Flagler County, and West Volusia/DeLand. The Port Orange office is the closest to Oak Hill. New agents get in-house marketing at no cost, seven-day non-competing manager support, structured training, and the global Leading Real Estate Companies of the World referral network.

What is your next step?

Read the licensing guide, explore the area with our Oak Hill parks and recreation guide, go deeper on the town’s real story in our full history of Oak Hill, then start a conversation with Adams, Cameron & Co. No pressure, just a clear picture of the path.
